key_insight: Open-source LLMs can convert unstructured liver-disease clinical notes into structured longitudinal data at scale, enabling reconstruction of patient trajectories.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help researchers analyze chronic liver disease and liver cancer risk factors faster by turning routine free-text records into usable datasets.
method: Manually annotated 507 reports from 30 patients to benchmark 4 open-source LLMs across 73 extraction tasks.
Compared constrained decoding versus unconstrained prompting across 5,590 prompt-output pairs.
Applied the best pipeline to 22,493 reports from 835 transplanted patients to generate structured variables and timelines.
evidence_signal: Llama 3.3 70B was the top performer, exceeding 90% accuracy on 59 of 73 tasks, and constrained decoding achieved >99.9% format adherence.
watch_item: Results come from a single-center transplant cohort, so external validation is needed before broader clinical research use.
paper_title: LLM-based reconstruction of longitudinal clinical trajectories in chronic liver disease.
